current_answer: A newly verified funded-startup route is Vercel for Startups: an approved Startup Partner can unlock a partner-specific Flexible Commitment up to USD 30,000 for a Series A-or-earlier company applying within 12 months of its last funding round. It is not a direct pre-funded route: partner proof, a matching-domain email, a Vercel team, and a payment method are required; the commitment lasts up to one year or until used, has an AI Gateway cap, and standard billing follows. Individual applicants still have NLnet’s constrained open-technology grant route; eligible pre-funded startups still have Google Start’s USD 2,000 for 12 months.

catalogue_card.question: Is Vercel’s USD 30,000 credit really your startup’s route?
catalogue_card.text: Only if an approved partner can prove it. The Vercel offer is funded and partner-gated, the amount varies by partner, and the one-year commitment can become standard billing after it ends.

summary: Funded startups: Vercel for Startups can provide a partner-specific Flexible Commitment up to USD 30,000, but only through an approved Startup Partner and within 12 months of the most recent funding round.
Vercel requires proof of partner affiliation, a company website, matching-domain email, Vercel team, payment method, and no prior programme credit.
The Vercel commitment ends after up to one year or when used. AI Gateway may use no more than 50%; standard billing follows.

Individuals: NLnet is a verified open-technology project grant, not a general personal stipend. Pre-funded startups: Google Start remains USD 2,000 for 12 months for a startup that passes its published gates.
Cloudflare Tier 3 still describes a self-funded route while its general qualification list says funding within the last 12 months. That conflict remains unresolved.
uncertainty: Vercel’s amount depends on the Startup Partner arrangement, and the reviewed FAQ does not publish country coverage.
One verified open-technology grant does not establish global individual-grant coverage.
We have not mapped every country, fund-specific term, service exclusion, or unpublished deadline.
Cloudflare has not published an explanation reconciling its self-funded Tier 3 wording with its general recent-funding requirement.
